title: COMP 3721 Data Communications
subtitle: Weeks 1–2, preparing for Quiz 1 and Quiz 2
description: Everything from Lectures 01a, 01b, 01c, the Math Review and Lecture 02: definitions in the instructor's own wording, every worked number from the slides and exercise sheets, live signal and network widgets, and quizzes in the real format (true/false, fill in the blank, written response). Finish with the two mock quizzes and the one-page study note.
intro:
:::quiz Quiz format, from the instructor
Weekly quizzes are written in the lab, starting Week 2, on material from previous weeks. **Quiz 1 covers Lecture Notes 01a only** (data communications, networks, topologies, the Internet). Quiz 2 will cover 01b/01c (layering, TCP/IP, connecting devices) and Lecture 02 (signals). The sample quiz shows three question styles: **true or false**, **fill in the blanks**, and **short written response**. You may bring **one A4 page of study notes (single-sided, preferably hand-written) and a calculator**; the last lesson here is a draft of that page. Quizzes are 20% of the grade (10 quizzes) and there are no make-ups.
:::

steps.note: take it cold first to find the gaps (about 25 min)
five components and simplex / half-duplex / full-duplex are the classic true/false items
link counts (mesh n(n-1)/2, star n, bus 1 + n drop lines) and the advantage / disadvantage lists
each layer's job, PDU name and example protocols; the fill-in-the-blank favourite
T = 1/f with unit prefixes; do the 60 Hz and 200 us examples by hand
bandwidth = highest minus lowest, with the middle-frequency trick from E02
redo E01 and E02 on paper before checking
retake; aim for 90% or better, then do mock quiz 2
hand-write your one A4 page from this draft
